notes:
Fire 81 @16:44-16:49 EDT, cold client (preview_start reused=false). Red Sprint 2 green throughout; ttg 08:14 -> 05:31.
(1) THE WIDGET CLASS CENSUS CAN LOSE AN ENTIRE CLASS. GTC5 is present in the API's CategoryString and absent from the widget's .racerCategory set, because #51 HARGESHEIMER -- the group's only GTC5 entrant -- renders a blank class cell. Crucially the widget rendered 'GTC5' for this car at 16:22:40 (armed) and blank by 16:41:39, so this is a MID-SESSION MUTATION, not a static per-car data gap. See widgetClassCensusCanLoseAnEntireToken.
(2) THE STOPPED-CAR HYPOTHESIS IS FALSIFIED AS A SHORT TIMEOUT. #125 DEBUSMANN has been frozen at lap 9 with a byte-identical Last Time (01:27.749) from 16:40:56 to 16:47:26 -- 6m30s of not circulating -- while his Diff accumulated +6 -> +8 laps. He is unambiguously stopped and his Last Time is unambiguously populated. So 'stopped => blank Last Time' is not a rule at 6.5-minute dwell. #201 SHAH remains the sole blank. Two surviving hypotheses, both testable at this session's finish: a MUCH longer dwell timeout (#201 has been stopped ~14 min), or a laps-down threshold (#201 is +15 laps, #125 is +8). Prediction registered.
(3) API CORRUPTION IS PERSISTENT, NOT TRANSIENT. #865's BestLapTime '00:01:' in 8721134 is byte-identical on re-fetch 7 minutes later. A consumer cannot retry its way out of it. A strict anchored-pattern audit over both siblings (46 competitor-rows x 3 duration fields) found exactly ONE malformed value and ZERO malformed TotalTime, confirming apiCorruptedTimeString.scopeCheck.
(4) API STILL FROZEN, AND THE GAP IS WIDENING. Both Red Sprint 2 siblings report maxLaps=6 against a widget leader on lap 17 -- an 11-lap divergence, up from 6 laps at 16:40:56. Zero lap progress in either record across the fire. No new session IDs published.
(5) TWO MORE SILENT-NULL SCHEMA TRAPS WALKED FIRST-HAND. .GroupedSessions[].CategoryString returns null for all 7 groups (the group object's keys are exactly {Category, Sessions}; CategoryString is a SESSION field), and .Session.Competitors returned null for the 12th time. Both silent, both cold-start recurrences of documented traps. See apiGroupObjectHasNoCategoryString.
(6) ONE NEW DOM-SELECTOR TRAP, SELF-INFLICTED: the first probe of the fire used '.timingRow, .timingRowAlt' -- both invented -- and returned rowCount 0 with no error, on a page displaying 22 cars. Fifth DOM-selector trap today and the third to fail toward a plausible EMPTY answer.
(7) POSITIVE CONTROL: the API Categories-dict fallback prescribed by widgetCanRenderABlankClassToken.durableRule WORKS. #51's class resolved to GTC5 via .Session.Categories['7'].Name, on a second car in a different run group from the #711 case that produced the rule. || poll82 (17:07-17:10): cooldown poll, no transition. The day's capture is functionally complete -- the stop condition fired at 16:59:49 and the only remaining scheduled action is the summary write-up plus task disable, due on the first fire after 17:19:49. Two things worth carrying into that write-up beyond the confirmatory data: (1) the Red Sprint 2 post-teardown grid is CORRECT, which contrasts with Blue Sprint 2's rewound/wrong grid and downgrades leaderboardCanRewindDuringHold from a property of teardown to an intermittent hazard with no post-hoc discriminator; (2) the API traps are not just documentation notes, they are reliably re-triggered by any cold client and cost three round trips this fire alone, so the summary should carry a single canonical extractor snippet rather than prose descriptions of each trap.

sessionDurationFindings.blueWarmUp: timeToGo pinned 00:00:00 all session (no duration configured)
sessionDurationFindings.yellowWarmUp: clock+timeToGo == 00:29:59 constant while green (real 30-min countdown), but ttg snapped to 00:00:00 at the checkered with clock at 13:49 and still running
sessionDurationFindings.timeToGoIsAmbiguous: ttg==00:00:00 now confirmed to mean AT LEAST TWO different things: (a) no duration configured (Blue Warm-Up, ttg 0 for its entire green run), and (b) session over/checkered (Yellow Warm-Up). RULE FOR CAMERA CONTROL: never trigger on ttg==0; use the flag cell only.
sessionDurationFindings.lapsToGoIsSentinel: 9999 while a session is live (means not lap-limited); RESETS TO 0 in the idle state (poll 15). So lapsToGo==0 is ambiguous the same way timeToGo==0 is - never trigger on either. POLL 20 refinement: 9999 is restored at ARM time, BEFORE green - so 9999 means 'a session is loaded and not lap-limited', not 'a session is running'.
sessionDurationFindings.redWarmUp: clock+ttg == 00:29:59 constant while green (30:00 configured); at the checkered ttg snapped to 00:00:00 with clock at 14:19 and still advancing. Matches Yellow Warm-Up exactly. Two of three warm-ups ran ~14 min of a configured 30 - treat configured duration as an upper bound only.
sessionDurationFindings.clockRunsPastCheckered: CONFIRMED 4/4 sessions today: the timing clock does NOT stop at the checkered. Blue Sprint 1 read 00:31:06 at first Finish observation, past both its own configured 00:29:59 and the flag. A frozen clock is not the end-of-session signal; the flag cell transition to Finish is.
sessionDurationFindings.clockResetsInIdle: NEW poll 15: post-checkered clock behavior has TWO phases - (1) keeps advancing past the checkered, then (2) resets to 00:00:00 when the widget tears the session down (~5-11 min after the checkered here). So neither a running clock nor a zeroed clock identifies session state on its own.
sessionDurationFindings.blueSprint1: RESOLVED at 11:10:28. Ran its FULL 30:00 window plus a lap-completion tail, taking the checkered at clock 00:31:06 (green 10:39:22). Confirms the session-type split: the two timed WARM-UPS took the checkered at 13:49 and 14:19 of an identical 00:29:59 configured window, while the RACE consumed all of it. Configured duration is an upper bound for warm-ups but a real duration for sprints. Camera control must not generalize warm-up run length to race sessions.
sessionDurationFindings.ttgCountdownShapeDiscriminatesEndType: NEW (poll 27/27b). timeToGo reaching 00:00:00 happens two distinguishable ways. (a) SNAP: ttg jumps from a large value straight to 0 at the checkered - both timed warm-ups did this (Yellow 00:21:15 -> 0, Red 00:20:11 -> 0), meaning the session was ended early by race control. (b) NATURAL DECREMENT: ttg counts smoothly down through small values to 0 - Blue Sprint 1 read 00:00:23 at 11:08:58 and 00:00:00 at 11:10:28, meaning the session ran its scheduled time. The DELTA of ttg between polls, not its value, carries this information. Still never trigger on ttg==0 itself (three-way ambiguous: no duration configured / ended early / ended on time).
sessionDurationFindings.timedRaceHasPostTtgZeroTail: NEW and directly camera-relevant (poll 27b). In a timed RACE the checkered does not fly when ttg hits zero - it flies when the LEADER NEXT CROSSES THE LINE. ttg reached 0 at approximately 11:09:21 (extrapolated: clock 00:29:36 at wall 11:08:58, configured 00:29:59); the Finish flag was up by 11:10:28, with leader #66 having advanced 20 -> 21 laps in between. That is a ~67 second tail, on the order of one lap (#66's lap 21 took 01:30.491). A camera controller that stops shooting at ttg==0 would miss the entire final lap INCLUDING the checkered-flag crossing - the single highest-value shot of the session. Budget at least one full lap of the leader's pace after ttg zero, and end on the flag cell, never on the clock.
sessionDurationFindings.poll52ConfiguredDurationIsExactly30m: Red Sprint 1, read at ARM with the clock still reading 00:00:00: ttg == 00:30:00 EXACTLY. Every prior measurement today came out as 00:29:59 because it was derived as clock+ttg after the clock had already ticked at least one second. So the configured duration is a round 30:00 and the recurring '29:59' in earlier entries is a one-second artifact of the derivation, not a real off-by-one in the timing system. DURABLE RULE: read the configured duration during the ARMED_PRE_GREEN window, where ttg is the raw configured value and the clock has not started. Deriving it as clock+ttg mid-session is correct to within a second but is not exact, and (per the warm-up sessions) tells you nothing about the actual run length anyway -- configured duration remains an UPPER BOUND that sessions may or may not consume.
sessionDurationFindings.poll63ArmedWithoutDuration: OPEN ANOMALY. For the first time today a session armed WITHOUT a configured duration visible: Blue Sprint 2 held clock 00:00:00 and ttg 00:00:00 for >=2m56s while otherwise fully armed. Every prior session today showed clock+ttg == 00:29:59 at arm, which is how configured duration was derived at all. So the clock+ttg arithmetic that produced '00:29:59' four times is NOT available at every arm, and Blue Sprint 2's configured duration is currently UNKNOWN rather than assumed-30-minutes. Do not carry the 29:59 constant forward as though it were a property of the event; re-derive it per session once ttg populates, and record it as unknown until then. See armedPreGreenState.CORRECTION_poll63 for the two competing explanations and the discriminating test.  [RESOLVED at poll 63b, 14:21:59.] Blue Sprint 2's configured duration IS 00:29:59 (clock 00:07:18 + ttg 00:22:41), identical to the other four timed sessions today. It was simply not yet published at arm time. So the 29:59 constant does hold for this session after all -- but the lesson stands unchanged: it was UNKNOWABLE for ~3 minutes of a genuine armed state, so it must be re-derived per session and recorded as unknown until ttg populates, rather than assumed from the pattern.
sessionDurationFindings.poll65_earlyTerminationIsNotRare: Blue Sprint 2 ran 00:26:16+ of its 00:29:59 configured window and was terminated UNDER CAUTION. This is the FOURTH session today to stop short of its configured duration (Blue Warm-Up, Yellow Warm-Up ~13:49/30:00, Red Warm-Up ~14:19/30:00, now Blue Sprint 2 ~26:16/29:59), against two that ran essentially full (Yellow Sprint 1, Red Sprint 1 at 00:30:36). Configured duration is confirmed for the FOURTH time as an UPPER BOUND, never a schedule.
sessionDurationFindings.newMechanismObserved: Previous short sessions were short for unknown reasons (assumed race-control discretion on warm-ups). This one has an OBSERVED cause: a full-course caution was flying with ~5 minutes to go and the session was called rather than restarted. That is a mechanism a predictor can actually use -- see whiteFlagFinalLapState.poll65_NEGATIVE_RESULT_yellowTerminatedSession.requiredMitigation.
sessionDurationFindings.predictiveConsequence: projectedNextCheckered-style arithmetic (green + configured + one leader lap) OVERPREDICTED this finish by ~5m13s (predicted ~14:46:10, actual 14:40:57). The method was validated on Red Sprint 1 to within a minute, so it is sound for full-distance sessions and simply has no way to anticipate a caution-shortened one. Any projection must therefore be published with an explicit 'assumes no further caution' qualifier, and must be revised DOWNWARD the moment a caution is observed in the closing minutes.

This directly confirms the flag word contributes exactly one occurrence and all remaining color-word hits are livery noise - i.e. a color-word text grep cannot isolate flag state even in a small 9-car field. POLL 15 second natural experiment: body-text "finish" went 1 -> 0 when the flag text blanked, confirming the flag word was the sole source of that token; green stayed at 1 (car #01 GREEN/BLACK livery). POLL 20->21 THIRD natural experiment: body-text 'green' went 1 -> 2 across the ARMED->GREEN transition, the +1 being the flag word and the residual 1 being car #12 PAUL AMICO's GREEN livery. Also note livery noise scaled with field size exactly as predicted - in this 21-car Blue group the idle-state baselines are yellow=3, red=3, black=3, white=4, blue=4, versus yellow=2/black=2/white=4 in the 9-car Red group. Prior polls could attribute drift to field size or membership churn; this one cannot. The livery noise floor is not stable even under a completely static session state, so no threshold or delta on a color-word grep can be made reliable. Structural selection of the bold .timingHeader child is mandatory, not merely preferred. POLL 27->27b FOURTH natural experiment, and the cleanest: across the Green->Finish transition body-text 'green' went 2 -> 1 and 'finish' went 0 -> 1, while yellow/red/black/white/blue held EXACTLY constant at 3/3/3/3/2. The flag word contributes precisely one occurrence and the livery floor was static across the very transition a detector would need to catch. That the floor happened to be stable here does not rescue text-grep - poll 25 showed it drifting with no state change at all - but it does cleanly isolate the flag word's contribution as exactly 1. POLL 36 - LIVERY FLOOR AT MAXIMUM FIELD SIZE: in this 28-car Yellow group the post-checkered body-text color-word counts are red=6, black=9, white=8, blue=5, yellow=1, green=1, purple=1, orange=2. Compare the 9-car Red group (yellow=2, black=2, white=4) and the 21-car Blue group (yellow=3, red=3, black=3, white=4, blue=4): the noise floor scales roughly with field size as predicted. The sharpest illustration yet is that the flag here IS white (Finish) yet contributes ZERO occurrences to any color-word bucket - the word rendered is "Finish" - while black=9 and white=8 sit in the body text purely as livery. A detector keying on the word "white" would be 8 false positives deep in the exact state where the real flag is white. Field size is set by the run group, so the worst noise coincides with the largest and most photographically interesting sessions. POLL 37 IDLE-STATE DATA POINT: with the flag word gone entirely (finish=0, flag=0, caution=0) the 28-car body still carries black=9, white=8, red=6, blue=5, silver=5 as pure livery noise, and the residual green=1 / yellow=1 are car liveries too. So in idle -- the state a detector most needs to distinguish from a live green -- a color-word grep returns a rich set of hits and zero signal. POLL 46 - NEW FALSE-POSITIVE CLASS (DRIVER NAMES): the noise floor is not only liveries. The 28-car retained body contains '#0 JARED RODEHEAVER', and 'JaRED' carries the substring 'red'. Measured directly this fire: a loose /red/gi over document.body.innerText returns 6 matches, a word-boundary /\bred\b/gi returns 5. The 5 word-boundary hits are all livery strings (RED / P 04 BOXSTER S, BLUE/WHITE/RED x2, RED / 99 BOXSTER x2); the 6th loose-only hit is a driver's FIRST NAME. Two consequences. (1) The false-positive floor is entry-list-dependent in a second, independent way -- it now varies with the NAMES in the field, not just the paint schemes, so it can never be calibrated as a per-field-size constant. (2) Adding word boundaries removes ONLY the name-substring class and leaves the entire livery class intact -- it is a partial mitigation that looks like a fix, which is the more dangerous failure mode. This is the same trap as the CLAUDE.md Syntactic-Semantic Seam Rule's substring-vs-token family: 'red' as a substring cannot carry the semantic distinction 'the red flag is out'. Read the flag carrier node; never grep the body, with or without boundaries.

CORRECTION_poll63.durableRule: Key ARM detection on lapsToGo 0 -> 9999 plus grid freshness, never on ttg. Treat ttg as a value to RECORD, not a state bit to BRANCH ON. Same failure shape as the flag-carrier text/color disagreement in idle: two fields that usually move together, documented as one composite signature, then observed moving independently -- so each field needs its own disposition rather than being folded into a single test.

RESOLVED_poll63b.resolvedAt: 2026-08-08T14:21:59-04:00, ~7 minutes after the correction was registered
RESOLVED_poll63b.answer: A VARIANT OF HYPOTHESIS A. ttg does populate -- it is not a differently-configured session. At 14:21:59 the clock read 00:07:18 and ttg read 00:22:41, summing to 00:29:59, identical to the four other timed sessions today. Since green was 14:14:41 and the last zero-ttg probe was 14:14:09, ttg populated inside that 32-second window, i.e. LATE in the arm and close to green.
RESOLVED_poll63b.soTheArmIsNonAtomic: Confirmed. ARM phase 1 (name + lapsToGo sentinel + fresh all-zero grid) began at or before 14:11:13 and held for ~3 minutes with ttg at 00:00:00 across four probes. ARM phase 2 (ttg populated from configured duration) landed between 14:14:09 and 14:14:41. Green followed immediately.
RESOLVED_poll63b.butDoNotOvergeneralizeTheTiming: It is tempting to conclude 'ttg populates ~30s before green'. Yellow Sprint 1 contradicts that: its arm at 11:16:38 ALREADY showed ttg 00:30:00 and green did not come until 11:19:40, a full 3m02s later. So the gap between ttg population and green ranges from <=32s to >=3m02s across two observations. What is durable is the ORDERING (ttg populates at some point during the arm, before green) and the fact that phase 1 can persist for minutes with ttg at zero. The LATENCY between the two is not characterized and should not be relied on.
RESOLVED_poll63b.whyTheOriginalRuleStillStands: The revised ARM signature does NOT need revising again. ttg remains disqualified as an ARM indicator precisely because it is a phase-2 property with an uncharacterized delay: an extractor gating on ttg > 0 would still have missed ~3 minutes of a genuine armed state here. lapsToGo 0 -> 9999 plus grid freshness caught it immediately. If anything this strengthens the rule -- ttg turns out to be a valid GREEN-IMMINENT hint but a useless ARM detector, which is exactly the 'record it, do not branch on it' disposition already recorded.
RESOLVED_poll63b.newSecondaryUse: ttg transitioning 00:00:00 -> nonzero while lapsToGo is already 9999 is a candidate GREEN-IMMINENT precursor worth testing on Yellow Sprint 2 and Red Sprint 2. Observed lead time 32s here, but >=3m02s on Yellow Sprint 1, so treat as unvalidated until it has been bracketed on more sessions.

postCheckeredHoldState.stopConditionImplication: DIRECTLY CONTRADICTS this capture task's own documented stop heuristic ('results frozen across consecutive polls'). Use the flag cell transition to Finish as the end-of-session signal; use lapsToGo 9999->0 plus clock reset to detect teardown.

Any camera-control timeout keyed to it (for example give up on a session after 10 minutes of Finish) would have mis-fired here by nearly half an hour.
poll70_OUTLIER.correlate: This was also the only caution-terminated session of the day and the only hold to show flag oscillation. The plausible reading is that the timing crew was actively reviewing/adjusting results during the hold -- which is consistent with BOTH the flag flutter AND the leaderboard rewind, and would make long holds a property of DISPUTED or INCIDENT-AFFECTED sessions rather than a random tail. NOT established; it is one instance, and the causal claim is unverified.
poll70_OUTLIER.durableRule: Never time-bound the post-checkered hold. lapsToGo 9999 -> 0 is the ONLY sound teardown signal, and a detector must be willing to wait indefinitely for it. Confirmed across four sessions spanning 2m39s to 38m41s -- a 14x spread.

poll82_redSprint2_TWO_PHASE_END_TO_END.headline: FIRST end-to-end capture of the poll-58 two-phase hold model inside a single fire, and it refines the model: the two phases are separated by an observable QUIET GAP, not run together.

phase1_trailingCarsStillTakingTheChecker.evidence: #01 GARRETT KRIEGER 21 -> 22 laps between the 16:54:47 and 16:55:11 probes -- the last car to take the checkered. His Diff also flipped from the string '+1 lap' to the numeric '1:26.259' as he joined the 22-lap block, and #127 GARRISON inherited the '+1 lap' marker one row down.
phase1_trailingCarsStillTakingTheChecker.sideEffect: A clean live instance of diffIsAPerLapBlockAccumulatorNotTimeBehindLeader: when KRIEGER left the 21-lap block its leader became GARRISON, and #277 BURKE's Diff re-based 48.598 -> 27.232 without BURKE moving. Diff is per-lap-block and mutates when the block's leader changes, not only when the car does.

quietGap.evidence: Grid byte-static on BOTH Laps and LastTime across the whole interval. Every one of the 22 rows identical.
quietGap.significance: NEW. Poll 58 described phase 1 flowing into phase 2; this fire shows a measurable all-static interval between them. So 'the grid stopped changing' is NOT a sufficient test that the hold is over -- a consumer sampling at >55s could see two static reads bracketing this gap and wrongly conclude teardown had occurred while phase 2 had not even started. This is a FIFTH independent failure mode for frozen-results-based stop conditions.

phase2_coolDownInLaps.evidence: LastTime mutated for 3 cars at 16:56:56 (#17 01:22.270->02:17.571, #228 ->02:05.386, #722 ->02:13.668), 9 more at 16:57:43, 6 more at 16:58:25, 1 more at 16:59:49 -- 19 of 22 cars eventually posted an in-lap. EVERY Laps value stayed frozen at the final classification throughout.
phase2_coolDownInLaps.stillMutatingAtTeardown: #777 PRAY posted 03:49.469 between 16:58:25 and 16:59:49, i.e. the grid was STILL mutating in the final 84s before teardown. Phase 2 does not settle before the teardown fires.

poll82_redSprint2_TWO_PHASE_END_TO_END.threeCarsNeverPostedAnInLap: #125 DEBUSMANN (frozen at lap 9), #201 SHAH (frozen at lap 2, blank LastTime) and #400 DUNIGAN retained their last racing values. Consistent with cars that were already stopped -- they cannot post a cool-down lap.
poll82_redSprint2_TWO_PHASE_END_TO_END.holdDuration: (3m38s, 6m52s], point estimate ~5m30s. Sits inside the 3m37s-6m32s band from the four earlier normal finishes; Blue Sprint 2's >8m06s remains the sole outlier and is now more confidently attributed to its caution-shortened ending (see finishIsNotTerminal.poll82_NORMAL_FINISH_DOES_NOT_REVERT).
poll82_redSprint2_TWO_PHASE_END_TO_END.cameraControlImplication: The ~4-6 min post-checkered window is confirmed on a 6th session and is a sound planning assumption. But a controller must not use grid stability to detect its end -- the quiet gap makes that ambiguous. Only the teardown signal is reliable.

sessionNameDoesNotIdentifyRunGroup.evidence: The widget header read 'Session: Sprint 1' for the Blue run group (21 entries, 911CUP/E/GT4/SP2/SP3/VGTO/VO/VU) from 10:38 to 11:14, and then read the byte-identical 'Sprint 1' for the Yellow run group (29 entries, SPB/SPC/G/J/ME1) from 11:16. The three morning warm-ups likewise all read 'Warm-Up'.
sessionNameDoesNotIdentifyRunGroup.impact: Session NAME cannot be used to detect a session change, identify a run group, or key a config lookup - three different run groups share one name within a single day. The API's CategoryString DOES carry the class list and is the only place the run group is expressed, but the API is lagged/stubbed and unusable live.
sessionNameDoesNotIdentifyRunGroup.cameraControlImplication: A per-series flag-interpretation config keyed on session name would silently apply the wrong series' rules. Key on field composition (car numbers / class codes present in the leaderboard) instead, or on a name+field-hash composite. This is a concrete requirement for the docs/todo.md 'Per-series flag interpretation config' work this capture effort feeds.
sessionNameDoesNotIdentifyRunGroup.relatedRule: Instance of the CLAUDE.md Syntactic-Semantic Seam Rule: 'Sprint 1' is a syntactic token being asked to carry the semantic distinction 'which run group', and it cannot.

idleDurationIsVariable: Observed idle durations today: ~24m (pre Blue Sprint 1), ~1m52s (pre Yellow Sprint 1), 1h08m26s (lunch, pre Red Sprint 1), ~23m28s (pre Blue Sprint 2), 13m52s-18m14s (pre Yellow Sprint 2). Range spans 1m52s to 68m26s -- nearly 37x. Idle duration carries NO predictive information about when the next arm comes; only the posted schedule does, and only loosely.

apiFieldTypesAreStrings.evidence: In SessionDetails.SortedCompetitors[], the fields Position, Laps, LastLapTime, BestPosition, BestLap, BestTime, TotalTime, Number, Transponder, Nationality, AdditionalData and Category are ALL JSON strings. Only ID, SessionID and RaceID are numbers.
apiFieldTypesAreStrings.trap: A jq `max` over [.SortedCompetitors[].Laps] on session 8720307 returned "8" for a field whose true maximum is 21 - lexicographic string comparison, silently plausible. The same trap applies to sorting or thresholding on Position and Number.
apiFieldTypesAreStrings.rule: Cast Laps/Position/Number to int before any comparison, max, sort or threshold. Relevant to the CLAUDE.md data-capture rule: the source's own types must be enumerated, not assumed from the field's semantics.
apiFieldTypesAreStrings.alsoNote: LapTimes is always an empty array in this endpoint - per-lap detail is not exposed here for any session, complete or stubbed.

leaderboardOrderUnstableBeforeFirstLap.evidence: Two in-fire samples 23s apart, both with EVERY lap and best time still 00:00.000: #78 GENE RAYMONDI and #5 NOAH MAZZOLA appeared in the first and were absent from the second; #83 HOYT AMMIDON and #251 FARAZ AHMED were the reverse. Positions 11-18 reshuffled wholesale.
leaderboardOrderUnstableBeforeFirstLap.impact: Before any car has completed a lap, the leaderboard's ORDER and MEMBERSHIP are both arbitrary and mutating - not merely 'membership varies' (the existing poll-23 finding) but order too. Position number carries no information at all in this window.
leaderboardOrderUnstableBeforeFirstLap.cameraControlImplication: Do not read grid order, class leaders, or car-of-interest position from the widget until at least one lap is complete. Combined with the ARMED-state finding, the ARMED entry list is good for WHO is out there but useless for WHERE they are.

nonFlagEvents.detail: #78 GENE RAYMONDI (ME1) dropped from the field on lap 1 of Yellow Sprint 1. Present in API record 8720318 with blank LastLapTime; ABSENT from both API record 8720319 and the widget. The feed signals a retirement ONLY by removing the row - there is no DNF/status/retired field anywhere. Field 29 -> 28.

whiteFlagFinalLapState.signature: flag carrier UNCHANGED at 'Green'/rgb(0,255,0); timeToGo 00:00:00; timingClock still advancing; lapsToGo == 1 (not the 9999 sentinel). Leaderboard otherwise normal.
whiteFlagFinalLapState.duration: ~1m23s, equal to one leader lap (01:30.344 last / 01:26.916 best)
whiteFlagFinalLapState.whyItMatters: FIRST PREDICTIVE signal for the checkered found in this feed. Everything else observed today is coincident or lagging: the flag carrier flips AT the checkered, the API lags minutes, and timeToGo hitting 00:00:00 is ambiguous (it also reads 00:00:00 in idle, in untimed sessions and after a checkered). lapsToGo transitioning OFF the 9999 sentinel to a small integer is unambiguous and gives roughly one lap of advance warning - enough to pre-position cameras for the finish.
whiteFlagFinalLapState.detectionRule: lapsToGo != 9999 AND lapsToGo is a small positive integer AND flag == Green  =>  final lap(s) running, checkered expected in ~lapsToGo * leader lap time.
whiteFlagFinalLapState.caveats: Only observed once, on one timed sprint, with lapsToGo == 1 (never 2+). Unknown whether a lap-limited (rather than time-limited) session counts lapsToGo down from the start, and unknown behavior if a yellow falls during the final lap. Needs confirmation on the afternoon Sprint 2 sessions before being treated as reliable.

poll58_SECOND_OBSERVATION.signatureMatch: EXACT. flag carrier unchanged at 'Green'/rgb(0,255,0); ttg 00:00:00; clock still advancing (00:30:36); lapsToGo == 1, not 9999. Identical on every axis to the Yellow Sprint 1 observation.
poll58_SECOND_OBSERVATION.duration: ~37s to ~95s (vs ~1m23s on Yellow Sprint 1). Both are approximately one leader lap; #17's laps ran 01:21-01:22.
poll58_SECOND_OBSERVATION.lapsToGoSemanticsPinned: At 13:38:43 ltg==1 with the leader showing 22 COMPLETED laps, and he finished on 23. So ltg counts laps REMAINING FOR THE LEADER, and final lap count == laps-at-white-flag + ltg. This resolves an ambiguity the Yellow observation could not: there, ltg==1 was seen at 20 laps and the leader finished on 21, which is consistent with either reading.
poll58_SECOND_OBSERVATION.predictiveAccuracy: The poll-35 detectionRule ('checkered expected in ~lapsToGo * leader lap time') was tested live for the first time. At 13:38:43 it predicted the leader's line crossing at 13:38:43 + 01:21 = ~13:40:04. The leader's lap count actually incremented 22->23 between 13:39:59 and 13:40:20. The prediction landed inside the observed bracket.
poll58_SECOND_OBSERVATION.statusChange: UPGRADED from 'OBSERVED ONCE, needs confirmation on the afternoon Sprint 2 sessions' to CONFIRMED 2-for-2 across two run groups and two sessions. Still unconfirmed: lapsToGo values >1, lap-limited (rather than timed) sessions, and behaviour if a yellow falls during the final lap.
poll58_SECOND_OBSERVATION.remainingCaveat: Both observations are timed 30-minute sprints that ran their full window. A session cut short (as both morning warm-ups were) snaps ttg from a large value straight to zero -- whether ltg passes through a non-sentinel value in that path has NEVER been observed and should not be assumed.

poll65_NEGATIVE_RESULT_yellowTerminatedS.whatHappened: The session ended UNDER CAUTION. ttg snapped from 00:04:56 (observed 14:39:44, yellow) straight to 00:00:00 with the flag carrier going Yellow -> Finish. lapsToGo NEVER left the 9999 sentinel at any point -- not before, during or after.
poll65_NEGATIVE_RESULT_yellowTerminatedS.significance: This DIRECTLY SETTLES the remainingCaveat registered at poll 58: 'A session cut short snaps ttg from a large value straight to zero -- whether ltg passes through a non-sentinel value in that path has NEVER been observed and should not be assumed.' It does not. The answer is NO.
poll65_NEGATIVE_RESULT_yellowTerminatedS.consequenceForTheDetectionRule: The poll-35 detectionRule ('lapsToGo != 9999 AND small positive AND flag == Green => final lap, checkered in ~ltg * leader lap time') is CORRECT WHEN IT FIRES but is NOT COMPLETE. It fires only on a session that runs its full timed window to a green-flag finish. On a session terminated early -- by a caution running to time, or by race control shortening it -- the ONLY predictive warning the feed offers is absent, and the Finish arrives with ZERO advance notice.
poll65_NEGATIVE_RESULT_yellowTerminatedS.severityForCameraControl: HIGH, and it is the most operationally important finding of the day. An automated controller that pre-positions for the finish on the lapsToGo signal alone would have MISSED this finish entirely. 3 of today's 8 sessions (both morning warm-ups and now Blue Sprint 2) ended before their configured window expired -- so the early-termination path is not an edge case, it is roughly 40% of sessions.
poll65_NEGATIVE_RESULT_yellowTerminatedS.requiredMitigation: Do not treat 'lapsToGo left 9999' as the finish predictor. Treat it as an OPPORTUNISTIC early-warning that is present on full-distance green finishes only. The controller must additionally be able to react to a Finish it did not see coming, and should treat ANY caution in the closing minutes of a session as raising the probability of an early ttg->0 termination. A useful heuristic falling out of this session: flag == Yellow AND ttg < ~1 leader lap => a green-flag restart is unlikely and the session will probably be called; go to finish-coverage posture immediately rather than waiting for a white flag that will never come.
poll65_NEGATIVE_RESULT_yellowTerminatedS.statusOfTheOriginalRule: Still CONFIRMED 2-for-2 on the sessions where it applies (Yellow Sprint 1, Red Sprint 1 -- both full-distance green finishes). Its SCOPE is now correctly bounded rather than its correctness being in doubt.
poll65_NEGATIVE_RESULT_yellowTerminatedS.remainingUnobserved: lapsToGo values > 1; genuinely lap-limited (rather than timed) sessions; and a caution that falls during a final lap already in progress (here the caution PRECEDED time expiry, so the white flag was never reached, which is a different case).

poll82_SECOND_CONSECUTIVE_MISS.what: lapsToGo read 9999 at 16:47:26 (prior fire's last probe, under Green) and 9999 again at 16:54:47 (this fire's first probe, under Finish). If the sentinel was released for a white-flag/final-lap window it fell entirely inside the 7m21s inter-fire gap and was NOT observed.
poll82_SECOND_CONSECUTIVE_MISS.why: Cron cadence. The prior fire ended at 16:50 and this one began at 16:54:25; the window sat in between. No tooling failure this time -- simply a gap.
poll82_SECOND_CONSECUTIVE_MISS.pattern: SECOND consecutive session whose white-flag window was lost. Poll 77 lost the previous one to a timed-out in-page sampling loop scheduled across the predicted ttg->0 instant. Different causes, identical blind spot.
poll82_SECOND_CONSECUTIVE_MISS.status: whiteFlagFinalLapState now rests on a SINGLE observed instance for the whole day. It is the most under-observed state in the record and the least safe to build a detector against.
poll82_SECOND_CONSECUTIVE_MISS.recommendationForNextTime: The white-flag window is predictable to within ~2 minutes from green + configured duration (ttg->0), and today that prediction was accurate to the second on every session. A future capture should tighten to sub-60s no-sleep probing for the ~4 minutes bracketing predicted ttg->0 -- NOT with a sleeping in-page loop, which is precisely what destroyed the poll-77 attempt.

poll77_FIRST_QUANTIFIED_MEASUREMENT.observation: At 16:13:06 the flag carrier read 'Finish'/rgb(255,255,255) while the P1 row still showed #247 JEFF SMITH on 19 laps, last 01:29.426. At 16:13:22 the same row showed 20 laps, last 01:29.082.
poll77_FIRST_QUANTIFIED_MEASUREMENT.inference: The checkered flies WHEN the leader crosses. So the crossing had physically happened before 16:13:06, the flag carrier already reflected it, and the leaderboard row did not render it for at least a further 16 seconds.
poll77_FIRST_QUANTIFIED_MEASUREMENT.lowerBoundOnly: 16s is a LOWER bound in both directions: the flag may have flipped before 16:13:06 (the prior probe was 16:11:52) and the row may have updated before 16:13:22. The true lag is somewhere in 0-90s and is not pinned by this measurement.
poll77_FIRST_QUANTIFIED_MEASUREMENT.whyItMatters: This upgrades flagLeadsLeaderboard from an ordering claim to a quantified one, and it is the correct direction for camera control: the flag carrier is the EARLIEST signal in the widget, earlier even than the leaderboard row for the same physical event. An extractor should key on the flag carrier and should never wait for leaderboard corroboration before acting -- corroboration arrives tens of seconds late.

lapsToGoSemantics: RESOLVED (was: '9999 sentinel'). 9999 means 'no lap limit in effect'. It holds during ARMED_PRE_GREEN, all of green-flag running on a timed session, and again from the checkered through idle. It drops to a real count ONLY in the final-lap window between time expiry and the checkered, then reverts to 9999. So ltg is a two-state signal in practice: 9999 = not-final-lap, anything else = final lap(s) in progress.
nextExpectedSession: NONE. Red Sprint 2 was the last posted Saturday session and teardown completed at 16:59:49. The widget has held a byte-identical IDLE across poll81/82/83 (17:00:08 -> 17:16:35, 16m46s). No ARMED re-entry expected. Cooldown expires 17:19:49; the next fire at or after that time must write the markdown summary and disable the task.

leaderboardPersistsThroughTeardown.finding: At idle teardown every header timing field zeroes (clock 00:00:00, ttg 00:00:00, lapsToGo 0, flag text blank) but the leaderboard remains FULLY POPULATED with the final 28-car classification. elemCount 810, 28 rows.
leaderboardPersistsThroughTeardown.implication: Idle is a HEADER-ONLY reset. Any detector that infers 'a session is live' from a populated/non-empty leaderboard will read as live for the entire lunch break and every inter-session gap. Liveness must come from the header (flag carrier text non-empty, or clock advancing), never from row presence.
leaderboardPersistsThroughTeardown.consistentWithDryRun: Matches the 2026-08-07 pre-event dry run, where the idle widget was showing Friday's frozen Qualifying results -- same mechanism, now observed across an actual live-to-idle transition rather than inferred.

redSprint2.finding: Re-confirmed on the day's final teardown, 10 minutes in and from a cold client: header fully zeroed, 22-row final grid fully populated and correct. The header-only-reset model of idle has now held on every teardown observed today.
redSprint2.quantified: Broad all-element class-token sweep returned 29 distinct tokens, identical to the running census, with no token appearing or disappearing at teardown. Row-selector hits 88 against a true field size of 22 -- a reminder that leaderboardRowCountIsNotFieldSize applies to the idle grid exactly as it does to a live one, because the substring selector [class*=row] also matches row1/row2/row3 sub-elements.

apiFinalResultsSessionId.finding: Blue Sprint 1 is published under THREE session IDs: 8720237 (epoch 1786199705, 21 cars, KAEMPF Laps=1), 8720238 (epoch 1786200139, 18 cars, KAEMPF Laps=1) and 8720307 (epoch 1786200139, 19 cars, KAEMPF Laps=21, best 01:26.076). Only 8720307 carries the FINAL classification, and it matches the widget's final Blue Sprint 1 state exactly (19 rows, #66 KAEMPF, 21 laps, 01:26.076).
apiFinalResultsSessionId.model: The API emits early frozen in-progress snapshots during a session, then a separate final-results session ID afterwards. The partial snapshots are never backfilled -- they stay frozen at the lap count they were captured at.
apiFinalResultsSessionId.EPOCH_SORT_IS_BROKEN: 8720307 (final) and 8720238 (stale partial) share the IDENTICAL SessionStartDateEpoc 1786200139. Epoch is NOT unique and does NOT distinguish final from partial. This capture task's documented rule ('always use the highest SessionStartDateEpoc') cannot separate them -- it picks arbitrarily by sort stability.
apiFinalResultsSessionId.durableRule: Among epoch ties prefer the HIGHEST session ID, and sanity-check by comparing max(Laps) across SortedCompetitors against the widget. Better still: treat the REST API as an after-the-fact results archive and the widget as the only live source.
apiFinalResultsSessionId.publishLagForFinal: Blue Sprint 1 took its checkered at 11:10:28; 8720307 was first observed at 11:57 (it was absent from the poll-36 listing at 11:54). So the final-results ID lands roughly 35-47 min after the checkered.

PUBLISH_LAG_CORRECTION.supersedes: publishLagForFinal ('the final-results ID lands roughly 35-47 min after the checkered', premised on 8720307 being 'absent from the poll-36 listing at 11:54')
PUBLISH_LAG_CORRECTION.finding: 8720307 is present in the jsonl capture log at 2026-08-08T11:20:54-04:00. Blue Sprint 1 took its checkered at 11:10:28, so the real observed publish lag for the final-results ID is ~10m26s (upper bound; it may have landed earlier, between the 11:17:09 poll where it is absent and 11:20:54 where it appears -- a 3m45s bracket giving a lower bound of ~6m41s).
PUBLISH_LAG_CORRECTION.howTheErrorHappened: The poll-37 note inferred absence from a poll-36 log line that simply did not restate 8720307. NOT-MENTIONED WAS READ AS ABSENT. The poll-36 line was a widget-focused capture; it never claimed the session listing lacked the ID.
PUBLISH_LAG_CORRECTION.methodRule: A per-poll log line is a record of what was captured, not an exhaustive census. Never derive a negative ('X was absent at time T') from a log line that was not explicitly recording presence/absence of X. Absence claims need a field that positively enumerates the set -- e.g. apiSessionCount or a full ID list -- not the lack of a mention.
PUBLISH_LAG_CORRECTION.consequenceRightNow: With the corrected ~10m precedent, Yellow Sprint 1's final-results ID is ~23 min OVERDUE at poll 44 (checkered 11:51:05, still session count 28 at 12:26). Final-results publish delay is therefore ALSO variable (>=2.3x spread already), joining in-progress publish lag (~9 min to ~30 min) as unusable for timing anything.
PUBLISH_LAG_CORRECTION.cameraControlImplication: Reinforces the standing rule from a new direction: not only is the API's CONTENT untrustworthy live, its PUBLISH TIMING has no bound tight enough to derive a session-end signal from. Only the widget's flag carrier + lapsToGo teardown is usable.

apiFinalResultsSessionId.duplicateEpochCensus_poll45: Full 28-session listing contains exactly TWO duplicate-epoch pairs: {8718867, 8718885} @1786129177 (yesterday) and {8720238, 8720307} @1786200139 (today). The live-relevant pair is the second: 8720238 is a Blue Sprint 1 in-progress STUB and 8720307 is the Blue Sprint 1 REAL FINAL, and they share an identical epoch. The final-results record was therefore published carrying the SAME epoch as one of its own in-progress stubs, not a later one.
apiFinalResultsSessionId.testablePrediction_poll45: If Yellow Sprint 1's final results follow the Blue precedent, they will appear under a NEW session ID but with epoch 1786202566 or 1786202132 -- matching an existing stub -- rather than a new later epoch. CHECK THIS on the fire where the Yellow final first appears. If it holds, epoch is structurally incapable of distinguishing stub from final even as a tiebreaker, and selection MUST be (Name, CategoryString) grouping plus content inspection (maxLaps, blank-Laps count, LastLapTime population).

coldClientIdleReproduction.finding: This poll opened a FRESH browser instance (preview_start returned reused=false, i.e. a cold page load, not a re-read of a long-lived tab) and got the IDENTICAL idle state: 28-row Yellow Sprint 1 leaderboard fully retained, header zeroed (clock 00:00:00, ttg 00:00:00, lapsToGo 0), flag carrier present at child index 6 with empty text and retained color rgb(255,255,255).
coldClientIdleReproduction.whyItMatters: It rules out the main competing explanation for the idle text/color DISAGREEMENT -- that the retained white was leftover client-side DOM from the prior Finish which a fresh client would not reproduce. It is served state. An extractor connecting cold, mid-gap, will see exactly this: a full stale leaderboard, a zeroed header, and a white flag carrier with no text. Treating empty carrier text as IDLE is therefore mandatory for cold starts, not just for continuously-connected clients.
coldClientIdleReproduction.poll62: 2026-08-08T14:03-04:00: TWELFTH reproduction, again from a genuinely cold client (preview_start returned reused=false). Identical served state: 19-row Red Sprint 1 leaderboard fully retained, header zeroed (00:00:00 / 00:00:00 / lapsToGo 0), single bold flag carrier at header child index 6 with empty text and color rgb(255,255,255). Now reproduced across three different retained grids (Yellow 28-row, Blue 19-row, Red 19-row), so the behaviour is not specific to any one session's leftover DOM.

poll72.significance: THIRTEENTH reproduction, and the most consequential one -- the first cold-client read against a retained grid that is KNOWN TO BE WRONG.
poll72.whatWasServed: A fresh browser instance (preview_start reused=false) received: the 20-row Blue Sprint 2 grid in its rewound lap-13 shape, header zeroed (00:00:00 / 00:00:00 / lapsToGo 0), session name still 'Sprint 2', and the single bold flag carrier at header child index 6 with empty text and colour rgb(255,255,255).
poll72.identityCheckAgainstThePriorReads: Byte-identical to polls 69, 70 (teardown) and 71 on both discriminators used all day: the lap histogram (9 cars on 13, 7 on 12, one on 11, one on 10, two on 9) and the non-monotone tail ordering (P17 #171 laps=11, P18 #525 laps=9, P19 #753 laps=10, P20 #08 laps=9). The tail ordering is the stronger of the two -- it is a shape no correct classification would produce, so its exact reproduction rules out coincidental agreement.
poll72.whatThisUpgrades: leaderboardCanRewindDuringHold.poll70 established that teardown froze a wrong grid. That was consistent with two explanations: (a) the server holds the wrong grid, or (b) the connected client's DOM had drifted and would be corrected on reconnect. This read eliminates (b). The wrong classification is what the SERVER hands to any new connection.
poll72.consequenceForIngestion: Strictly worsens finalClassificationCanBeLostFromBothSources. A results-ingestion path cannot recover the true final by reconnecting, by opening a second client, or by waiting -- the wrong grid is authoritative-looking, stable, self-consistent in ordering, and served to everyone. The only recovery is to have captured the classification at or immediately after the checkered, which is what this capture did at 14:41:18.
poll72.methodNote: This reproduction was free -- it fell out of the ordinary per-fire cold start, not a designed experiment. Worth keeping in mind that every fire of this poller is incidentally a cold-client test, which is why the reproduction count is high.

poll82.significance: FOURTEENTH reproduction, and the useful counterweight to poll72. poll72 established that a cold client is served a KNOWN-WRONG retained grid (Blue Sprint 2, rewound to lap 13). This one establishes that a cold client is served a KNOWN-CORRECT retained grid for Red Sprint 2.
poll82.whatWasServed: Fresh browser instance (preview_start reused=false): 22-row Red Sprint 2 grid, header zeroed (00:00:00 / 00:00:00 / lapsToGo 0), session name still 'Sprint 2', single bold flag carrier with empty text and colour rgb(255,255,255).
poll82.correctnessCheck: Byte-matches the classification captured live at and immediately after the 16:52:57-16:54:47 checkered bracket on all three discriminators used for Red Sprint 2: field size 22, leader #17 CALZARETTA on 22 laps with best 01:19.690 set on lap 12, and the lap histogram (six cars on 22 through P6, first lap-down car at P7). No rewind, no truncation, no reordering.
poll82.whatThisSettles: Teardown-time grid corruption is NOT universal. Blue Sprint 2 froze wrong; Red Sprint 2 froze right. So leaderboardCanRewindDuringHold describes a real hazard with a real incidence rate, not a deterministic property of teardown. An ingestion path therefore cannot assume the post-teardown grid is either always trustworthy or always suspect.

This fire consequently mis-diagnosed it as a curl/sandbox file-write race and then as a possible rate-limit empty-body, and only isolated the true cause by bisecting the jq filter (.Successful OK -> length OK -> [.Laps|tonumber] FAILS -> per-record select). Parse per-row inside a try, count and log the coercion failures (the CLAUDE.md batch-error-counter rule), and never let the aggregate step (max/sum/length) be the first place a bad row surfaces. apiEndpointPathTrap.finding: POST to https://api.race-monitor.com/v2/Common/GroupedSessionsForRace (a plausible-looking wrong path) returns an ASP.NET 302 to /Home/Missing/?aspxerrorpath=... and, following redirects, an HTML body with a 200 status. The correct path is /v2/Results/GroupedSessionsForRace.
apiEndpointPathTrap.whyItMatters: A wrong or renamed endpoint does NOT surface as a 404. A consumer that checks only the HTTP status sees success and then fails at the JSON parse, or worse, treats a parse failure as 'no sessions yet' and silently reports an empty race.
apiEndpointPathTrap.durableRule: Never infer API success from the HTTP status code. A wrong path prefix yields 200 + text/html after a 302, which a naive client parses as a malformed-JSON error at a random column rather than as a routing mistake. Validate Content-Type is application/json AND .Successful is true before touching any payload field. Corollary for the confirmed endpoints: /v2/Results/GroupedSessionsForRace and /v2/Results/SessionDetails.
apiEndpointPathTrap.reproducedLive_poll45: 2026-08-08T12:29-04:00: walked into this trap first-hand and EXTENDED it. POST /v2/Common/SessionDetails returned HTTP 200 with a 171-byte text/html ASP.NET stub ('Object moved to /Home/Missing/?aspxerrorpath=/v2/Common/SessionDetails'), not a 404 and not JSON. So the trap belongs to the /v2/Common/ PREFIX generally, not to GroupedSessionsForRace specifically: SessionDetails lives under /v2/Results/ too. Both endpoints used all day are /v2/Results/*.

elemCountIsNotAChangeDetector.poll60_converseCase: Poll 60 supplies the CONVERSE of the earlier evidence and is the stronger half of the argument. Polls 47/50 showed elemCount CHANGING (810 -> 812 -> 810) with NO state change. Poll 60 shows elemCount NOT changing across a state change that did occur: it read 585 during live Red Sprint 1 (polls 57/58), 585 at the post-teardown idle (poll 59), and 585 again here. groupLevelKeysAreNotSessionLevelKeys.trapRecurrenceObservation: This is the SECOND consecutive fire in which a reader who had this state file's warning available still reached for the plausible names first (poll 58 hit .Groups/.SessionID; poll 59 hit group-level .Name/.CategoryString/.SessionEpoch). The only durable fix is procedural: dump keys() on the actual response before writing any field access, every fire. trapRecurrenceUnderColdStart.whyItMatters: Each fire is a cold session that reconstructs the queries from the plausible-sounding English field names rather than from the recorded schema. Documenting a trap in prose demonstrably does NOT prevent its recurrence -- all four failures were silent (200+HTML, or jq null/empty), so none of them announced itself as a schema mistake; three of the four initially read as 'the race has no sessions'.
trapRecurrenceUnderColdStart.durableRule: Do not ship this API access as prose-guided ad-hoc curl/jq. Write a single checked-in helper (one function per endpoint) that hardcodes the verified path prefix and field names and asserts Content-Type==application/json AND .Successful==true AND the expected key is present-and-non-empty before returning. The traps are only actually closed once they are unreachable by construction; per the CLAUDE.md syntactic-semantic seam rule, the schema needs one source of truth rather than being re-typed from memory at each call site.
trapRecurrenceUnderColdStart.severityForCameraControl: Not on the live-control path (the API is already ruled out as authoritative for flag state), but directly on the path for any post-session results ingestion.

So the assertion works as specified even when the field-name intuition fails, which is the first direct evidence that the proposed helper's CONTRACT (assert present-and-non-empty) is sufficient to contain this family -- as distinct from poll 63, which avoided the traps entirely by dumping keys() first. Two different mechanical defences have now each been shown to work once; the un-defended fires have failed nine times out of ten. SECOND OBSERVATION, on the non-API side: this same fire ALSO produced a first-pass wrong CONCLUSION about the leaderboard (calling the rewound grid 'coherent' without cross-checking LastTime against the already-recorded caution timeline; retracted in leaderboardCanRewindDuringHold.poll67_REWIND_STOPPED_WITHOUT_CONVERGING). That is the poll-63 counter-example reproduced: written-down CONCLUSIONS get re-derived carelessly by cold fires exactly like written-down FIELD NAMES do, and no keys()-style mechanical step exists to catch them. The analogous mechanical defence for conclusions is to cross-check any new claim against at least one INDEPENDENT quantity already in this file before recording it -- here, one comparison against cautionOnsetReconstructionFromLapTimes was enough to overturn it.

trapsWalked.how: POSTed /v2/Common/GroupedSessionsForRace. Returned HTTP 302, 179 bytes, non-JSON. Recovered on the next call by switching to /v2/Results/. Second time this exact prefix has been walked into.
trapsWalked.note: The failure presented EXACTLY as jqParseErrorMisdirection predicts -- 'jq: parse error: Invalid numeric literal at line 1, column 26' -- i.e. the message blamed the payload, not the route. The documented rule (validate non-empty body, then Content-Type, then .Successful, BEFORE touching any field) was applied on the retry and made the corrected call verifiably clean: 16244 bytes, application/json, Successful=true.

trapsWalked.how: Filtered session records on .SessionID / .SessionEpoch. The real field names are .ID and .SessionStartDateEpoc. The filter matched NOTHING and returned an empty result with no error -- the exact silent-empty signature the trap describes.
trapsWalked.note: Caught only because the follow-up keys() probe was run. The documented 'run keys() FIRST, before any field access' discipline was NOT followed on the first attempt this fire; it was run second, as recovery. Running it first would have cost one call and avoided a wrong intermediate reading.

poll68_tenthReproduction.runningTally: Ten fires have now re-walked at least one documented trap on a cold client; two fires (63, 65) were clean. Both traps this fire were recovered within the same fire, and neither reached the state file as a finding.
poll68_tenthReproduction.whatThisKeepsShowing: Cold-start trap recurrence is not decaying with the number of times the trap is written down. Every one of these traps shares a signature -- a wrong accessor produces a plausible EMPTY or MALFORMED result rather than an error -- and the documentation of them is not what prevents them; running the cheap structural probe FIRST is. The durable fix is procedural: keys() before field access, and the full validation chain before any parse, as unconditional first steps rather than as things to remember.

poll70_THIRD_CLEAN_FIRE.result: CLEAN on the API side -- zero documented traps re-walked. Correct /v2/Results/ prefix on the first call; keys() dumped at BOTH group level and session level before any field access; Successful + cardinality (groups=7, sessions=32) asserted before extraction. Third clean fire (63, 65, 70) against ten dirty ones.
poll70_THIRD_CLEAN_FIRE.whatWorked: Same mechanical cause as poll 63: the dump-keys()-first step was executed in the SAME tool call as the fetch, so there was no window in which a field name could be typed from intuition.
poll70_THIRD_CLEAN_FIRE.butNotCleanOverall: The fire still walked a trap of exactly this family -- just on the DOM side rather than the API side. It invented a nonexistent .racerNumber class and anchored the row join on .position.parentElement instead of .racerRowStacked, producing 20 well-formed rows with ten null columns and no error. See leaderboardCellClassSelectors.poll70_CORRECTION_ROW_ANCESTOR.
poll70_THIRD_CLEAN_FIRE.whatThisAdds: The keys()-first discipline is scoped to whatever surface the agent consciously classifies as the risky one. This fire applied it rigorously to the API, having read the trap log, and then joined a DOM tree from memory without any equivalent structural probe. The family is not an API family -- it is a wrong-accessor-returns-plausible-empty family, and it spans every schema-like surface in this system. The mitigation has to be surface-agnostic: probe the actual structure before writing any accessor, DOM included.

poll71_TWO_TRAPS_RE_WALKED_ENDING_THE_CL.context: Polls 68/69/70 were recorded as clean fires (zero documented traps re-walked). Poll 71 broke that streak with TWO in a single fire, both already documented, both walked within about 90 seconds of each other.

trapOne_silent.what: Counted sessions with jq '[.Groups[]?.Sessions[]?] | length' -- the correct key is .GroupedSessions[].Sessions[].
trapOne_silent.result: Returned 0. No error, exit status 0. The true count is 32.
trapOne_silent.whyItWasCaught: Only because the SAME command also printed keys() of the response, which showed ['Favorited','GroupedSessions','Successful'] and made the wrong key obvious on sight. Had the count been printed alone it would have been recorded as 'zero sessions', which for this endpoint reads as a plausible 'the race has no sessions yet'.
trapOne_silent.note: The '?' optional operators made it worse -- they suppress exactly the type error that would otherwise have surfaced the wrong key. Defensive jq syntax converted a loud failure into a silent one.

trapTwo_loud.what: Queried .Session.Competitors on SessionDetails -- the correct key is .Session.SortedCompetitors.
trapTwo_loud.result: jq: error 'Cannot iterate over null (null)'. Immediate, unmissable, cost one retry.

poll71_TWO_TRAPS_RE_WALKED_ENDING_THE_CL.theContrastIsTheLesson: Same class of error (a plausible field name that does not exist), same fire, same operator, ~90s apart -- and opposite detectability. The loud one cost a retry. The silent one would have entered the permanent record as a factual claim about the race. This is the third time today the file has recorded that pairing; it is now well past anecdote.
poll71_TWO_TRAPS_RE_WALKED_ENDING_THE_CL.whatActuallyDefendedTheFire: Not memory of the documented traps -- both were documented and both were walked anyway. What defended it was a METHOD: printing keys() and Successful alongside every extraction, and asserting a non-zero expected cardinality. That habit is mechanical, survives cold start, and does not depend on having read the trap list. Prefer strengthening it over adding more entries to the trap list.
poll71_TWO_TRAPS_RE_WALKED_ENDING_THE_CL.durableRuleReinforced: Never use jq's '?' operators on a first-time or cold-start extraction. Their purpose is to suppress type errors, which is precisely the signal that catches a wrong key. Use them only after the key path has been verified against a printed keys() on the same payload.

poll76_THREE_IN_ONE_FIRE.summary: This fire tripped THREE documented traps in a single run, all three failing silently or near-silently, despite having the state file's warnings available and having read several of them before writing the queries.

instances.novelty: NEW sub-trap, not previously catalogued: extrapolation of the real '<field>Value' suffix convention from the six row3 cells onto the four columns that do not follow it. Recorded as leaderboardCellClassSelectors.poll76_VALUE_SUFFIX_PATTERN_DOES_NOT_GENERALISE.

instances.novelty: 4th recurrence of an unchanged, explicitly documented trap

poll76_THREE_IN_ONE_FIRE.whatIsNewAnalytically: Prior entries framed this as 'API path traps recur at ~100% under cold start'. This fire shows the phenomenon is NOT specific to the API: the DOM instance has exactly the same shape (a plausible name derived from a partial convention, failing silently) and was hit in the same run. The generalisation is that ANY name in this system that a reader can plausibly guess will be guessed, and this codebase's naming is inconsistent enough that guessing is wrong more often than not.
poll76_THREE_IN_ONE_FIRE.whyReadingTheNotesDidNotHelp: The notes were read this fire -- flagCarrierSignature, rowSelectorCensus, leaderboardCellClassSelectors and stackedLayoutAndZeroViewportCaveat were all pulled BEFORE the second probe. The failure happened on the FIRST probe, written from intuition before the notes were consulted, which is the actual mechanism: the cost of looking up the selectors feels higher than the cost of guessing them, and the guess returns something plausible rather than an error, so the feedback that would correct the habit never arrives.
poll76_THREE_IN_ONE_FIRE.durableFix: Escalates the existing recommendation from 'pin the paths in code' to 'the probe script must not contain a hand-typed name at all'. Concretely: keep one canonical probe function holding all four API paths and all ten DOM selectors, with a startup assertion block (non-empty body; Content-Type JSON; .Successful true; .Session.SortedCompetitors non-empty; row 1 .racerName non-null; row 1 .racerCategory non-null; flag carrierCount == 1). Every one of this fire's three errors would have been caught by that block at the first call rather than by a later human noticing nulls.

poll77.one: apiEndpointPathTrap -- POSTed /v2/Common/GroupedSessionsForRace before /v2/Results/. Body failed jq with 'Invalid numeric literal at line 1, column 26', the jqParseErrorMisdirection signature. Content-Type was NOT captured on that call, so this is consistent-with rather than a re-measurement of the documented 302-to-HTML behaviour; recorded honestly as such.
poll77.two: apiWrongKeySilentZero -- see its poll77 entry. New shape: silent zero from a wrong top-level key on the CORRECT endpoint.
poll77.cumulativeObservation: Every fire today that started cold has tripped at least one documented trap. The traps that get tripped are consistently the ones where the failure LOOKS like a data condition (empty result, parse error) rather than a mistake -- which is precisely why the structural probe has to come first.

Surfaced as a jq 'Invalid numeric literal at line 1, column 26' -- exactly the misdirection jqParseErrorMisdirection describes. Third recurrence today of a trap documented in this file.

Assumed .Groups[].Sessions[] with .SessionID and .SessionEpoch. Actual: .GroupedSessions[].Sessions[] with .ID and .SessionStartDateEpoc (misspelled, no trailing 'h'). The wrong epoch key returned null on 36/36 sessions -- silent and uniform, the apiWrongKeySilentZero failure in its null flavour. It produced a plausible-looking table with 'epoch=null' in every row.

Guessed '.number', '.name', '.category' for the leaderboard row cells. All three returned null on 23/23 rows and the extractor produced a complete, well-formed 23-row result with every one of those fields null and no error raised.
