Key off car number, never off position, and re-read after green.
armedGridIsNotStatic_poll78.relationToClaudeMdRules: Instance of the Threshold-Boundary rule's ambiguous-input family: EMPTY vs ZERO vs ABSENT are three distinct cell states here and the arm state exhibits all three simultaneously in different columns of the same row.

scheduleRiskAssessment_poll78_SIGN_CHANG.corrects: scheduleRiskAssessment_poll70_CORRECTS_POLL69 and every projection built on it, all of which modelled today's schedule error as monotonically increasing lateness.
scheduleRiskAssessment_poll78_SIGN_CHANG.finding: The schedule error CHANGED SIGN between two consecutive sessions. Yellow Sprint 2 went green ~52 minutes LATE (posted 02:50p, green 15:42:26). Red Sprint 2 went green 12m02s EARLY (posted 04:35p, green 16:22:58). Swing of roughly 64 minutes across one session boundary.
scheduleRiskAssessment_poll78_SIGN_CHANG.mechanism: Almost certainly slack in the posted schedule rather than anything accelerating: Yellow Sprint 2 finished around 16:13 and Red Sprint 2 had a 1h45m posted gap after Yellow's 02:50p slot. Once the preceding session cleared, race control simply ran the next one. The posted times are a not-before floor for the FIRST session of a block and an ordering hint thereafter -- they are not predictions.
scheduleRiskAssessment_poll78_SIGN_CHANG.durableRule: NEVER extrapolate a running lateness offset forward. Today's offsets in order were roughly: on time, +5, +15, +30, +40, +52, -12 minutes. A camera-control scheduler must be event-driven off the widget's ARMED signal and must poll continuously through the whole race day; using the posted schedule to decide WHEN TO START POLLING would have missed the start of the final race of the day by 12 minutes.
scheduleRiskAssessment_poll78_SIGN_CHANG.consequenceForThisTask: The stop condition would have been reached without ever being observed if this task had used the posted 04:35p time to decide when to pay attention. It did not, because the task polls unconditionally on a 5-minute cron. Keep that design.

cellSelectorNullCensus_extension_poll78: Extend the existing null-census discipline to the row-IDENTITY selectors (.position, .racerName, .racerCategory), not just the six value cells. A misnamed identity selector is MORE dangerous than a misnamed value selector because the resulting record still has the right SHAPE -- correct row count, correct ordering, plausible structure -- and only the content is missing. Assert non-null on every selector for every row and fail loudly on any null.

cautionCrossCheckDetectorLagsPastTheCaut.severity: HIGH -- this CORRECTS a documented proposal in yellowFlagState.whyTheCorroborationMatters rather than confirming it.
cautionCrossCheckDetectorLagsPastTheCaut.whatTheProposalSaid: 'if the carrier says Green but the whole field is running 1.5-2x its best pace, one of the two signals is wrong and the system should degrade safely rather than trust either blindly.' It was qualified with 'the ratio lags the flag by up to one lap... so it confirms rather than predicts.'
cautionCrossCheckDetectorLagsPastTheCaut.whatActuallyHappened: The lag is not merely 'up to one lap' in the benign sense assumed; for a SHORT caution it exceeds the caution's own duration, so the detector's alarm window falls entirely on GREEN track. Measured this fire: at 16:29:13, flag = YELLOW, median inflation ratio 1.069 and max 1.258 -- the detector is NOT firing while the caution is actually flying. At 16:31:06, flag = GREEN (restart was 16:30:11), median 1.243 and max 1.515 -- the detector is AT PEAK, and 1.515 sits squarely in the proposed 1.5-2x alarm band, roughly 55 seconds after the track went green.
cautionCrossCheckDetectorLagsPastTheCaut.mechanism: Lap-block stratification. A car only posts its caution-slowed lap when it COMPLETES that lap. At 16:29:13 the 11 cars whose newest completed lap was lap 3 still showed clean green ratios (1.000-1.066) because their caution lap was still in progress; only the 10 cars already through lap 4 showed partial inflation (1.069-1.194). By 16:31:06 the ex-lap-3 cars had completed a full caution lap and reported 1.312-1.515. The detector therefore measures the caution one full lap AFTER the fact, and a caution shorter than ~1.5 lap times is entirely invisible to it while flying and maximally visible once it is over.
cautionCrossCheckDetectorLagsPastTheCaut.consequenceForTheProposedCrossCheck: As specified, the cross-check would have fired a 'signals disagree, degrade safely' alarm on a green track ~1 minute into a restart -- exactly the moment a camera controller most wants to be shooting green-flag racing. It produces a false alarm on EVERY short caution, and it is silent during the part of a caution when it would have been useful. It is not a safe general cross-check in the form documented.
cautionCrossCheckDetectorLagsPastTheCaut.revisedGuidance: Do not compare the inflation ratio against the CURRENT flag. If the ratio is used at all, compare it against the flag as it was ~1 leader-lap ago, i.e. treat it as a delayed corroborator on a lagged buffer, and never as a live contradiction detector. Better: for the specific job of catching a carrier that has gone stale or wrong, this metric is the wrong instrument entirely -- its phase error is on the same order as the events being detected. The carrier remains the only low-latency flag signal in this feed.
cautionCrossCheckDetectorLagsPastTheCaut.whatSurvivesFromTheOriginalFinding: The Blue Sprint 2 observation itself is unaffected and still correct: a field-wide simultaneous inflation of 1.5-2x really did indicate a caution, and no other mechanism plausibly produces it. What is corrected is only its proposed USE as a same-instant cross-check against the flag carrier.
cautionCrossCheckDetectorLagsPastTheCaut.testabilityNote: This was measurable only because the caution was short (~2-3 min) and the poll cadence happened to bracket it on both sides. The Blue Sprint 2 caution ran into the Finish, so its detector lag could never have been separated from the caution's own duration. Short cautions are the discriminating case; log ratio-vs-flag phase on any future one.

apiLaterSiblingCanLoseData.severity: HIGH -- it inverts the directionality assumption underneath apiProgressiveSnapshotChain AND underneath apiFinalResultsSelectionRule's highest-ID key.

data.delta: Across the 22 cars present in BOTH records, Position, Laps, BestLapTime and TotalTime are byte-identical for 21 of 22 cars. The 22nd (#865) differs only in a CORRUPTED BestLapTime (below). The single other change is that LastLapTime is wiped to the empty string on ALL 22. The two blank-Laps DNS entries (#45 FELKER, #551 PALMER) are pruned, consistent with poll65_minimalDeltaBetweenSiblings.
data.fetchHygiene: both fetched individually, HTTP 200, application/json, non-empty body, .Successful true, SortedCompetitors cardinality asserted (24 and 22)

apiLaterSiblingCanLoseData.finding: The later sibling contains STRICTLY LESS information than the earlier one. It advances the race by zero laps across a 16m26s epoc gap and it deletes an entire populated column. apiProgressiveSnapshotChain described the chain as one where 'competitor count and maxLaps all rise essentially monotonically together' and framed later snapshots as progressively richer. That is now falsified: a later snapshot can be a strict regression on content while still being the correct answer to 'which record is newest'.
apiLaterSiblingCanLoseData.whyItMattersForSelection: apiFinalResultsSelectionRule keys on highest-ID-within-(Name, CategoryString). Applied here, highest-ID picks 8721134 -- the record with 22 of 22 LastLapTime values missing and one corrupted BestLapTime -- over 8721133, which has 22 of 24 LastLapTime values present and an intact BestLapTime for the same car. The selection rule is still correct for RECENCY and this fire does not propose replacing it; the point is that recency and completeness are INDEPENDENT axes here, and a consumer that assumes the newest record dominates the older one field-by-field will silently discard data it already had.
apiLaterSiblingCanLoseData.durableRule: Do not treat API sibling records as a monotone refinement chain. When ingesting a session, MERGE across all siblings in the (Name, CategoryString) group field-by-field with a per-field non-empty preference, rather than taking the newest record wholesale. Concretely: take Position/Laps/TotalTime from the newest record, but for BestLapTime and LastLapTime prefer the newest NON-EMPTY, WELL-FORMED value across the chain. Log every field where an older sibling had a value the newest lacks -- that count is a data-loss metric, and this fire it would have been 22.
apiLaterSiblingCanLoseData.relationToClaudeMdRules: Data-Capture Backward-Chaining Rule. The failure mode is the documented one exactly: a field that is present in the source and silently absent from the output, with nothing in the payload marking the absence as meaningful. apiNoProvisionalFlag already established there is no field distinguishing a provisional record from a final one; this shows there is likewise no field distinguishing a record that LOST data from one that never had it.
apiLaterSiblingCanLoseData.openQuestion: Unknown whether the LastLapTime wipe is a one-off or a systematic property of later siblings. apiProgressiveSnapshotChain.poll64 independently recorded Blue Sprint 2's later sibling 8720632 with LastLapTime empty for 19 of 20 competitors -- but the earlier sibling 8720631 was never checked for the same field, so that case cannot distinguish 'wiped' from 'never populated'. Two of two later siblings examined today are near-totally blank on LastLapTime, which is suggestive. Re-check the EARLIER sibling's LastLapTime fill rate on every future chain, not just the later one -- that is the measurement both prior fires omitted.

apiCorruptedTimeString.severity: HIGH -- first observed instance today of the API emitting a MALFORMED value rather than a blank or a stale one, and it is silent-capable under lenient parsing.
apiCorruptedTimeString.observation: #865 FRANK VENEZIA, same competitor row in two sibling records of the same session: 8721133 has "BestLapTime":"00:01:29.514"; 8721134 has "BestLapTime":"00:01:". BestLap ("2"), Position ("18"), Laps ("5") and TotalTime ("00:08:50.908") are identical in both, so this is not a different lap being reported -- it is the same value, truncated in transit or in generation.
apiCorruptedTimeString.verification: Confirmed by hexdump-style inspection of the raw response bytes, not inferred from a parser. The literal string in 8721134 is 00:01: with a trailing colon and no seconds component. The surrounding JSON is well-formed and .Successful is true, so no transport or schema check catches it.
apiCorruptedTimeString.whyItIsDangerous: The string is well-formed JSON and syntactically resembles a duration. A STRICT duration parser raises -- which, per jqParseErrorMisdirection, will be reported against the input file at offset 0 and mislead the diagnosis toward transport. A LENIENT parser (split on ':', coerce each part, default missing parts to 0) yields 00:01:00 = 60.000s: a plausible-looking best lap 29.5 seconds faster than reality, which would rank #865 as comfortably the fastest car in a field whose real best is 01:19.690. The wrong answer is the quiet one.
apiCorruptedTimeString.durableRule: Validate every API duration against a strict anchored pattern (^\\d{2}:\\d{2}:\\d{2}\\.\\d{3}$) before use. Treat a non-matching NON-EMPTY string as its own typed outcome (malformed), distinct from both a blank field (apiBlankNumericFields) and a stale one (apiPartialSnapshotBestLapIsStale) -- three different conditions that a naive numeric coercion collapses into one. Never default missing time components to zero.
apiCorruptedTimeString.relationToClaudeMdRules: No-Log-Scraping / structured-signalling rule and the Data-Capture rule together. 'The field is malformed' is a distinction that must be carried as a typed branch; recovering it by pattern-matching how badly the string parses is exactly the inference the rule forbids. It also lands on the Threshold-Boundary rule's ambiguous-input list: this is a real, observed instance of the 'silent reasonable behavior on ambiguous input' family, found in production data rather than constructed for a test.
apiCorruptedTimeString.scopeCheck: This was the ONLY malformed duration in either record -- all other BestLapTime/TotalTime/LastLapTime values in both siblings either match the strict pattern or are the empty string. So it is rare, not endemic; that is precisely why an unguarded consumer would never notice it.
apiCorruptedTimeString.openQuestion: Cause unknown. It appeared in the LATER sibling of the pair, in the same record that wiped LastLapTime on all 22 cars, which hints the two are products of one bad generation pass rather than independent faults. Worth checking whether any other session's later sibling carries a truncated duration.

poll81_PERSISTENCE_CONFIRMED.answersOpenQuestion: Partially. This entry asked whether other later siblings carry truncated durations; that is still open. But it also left implicit whether the corruption was a transient serialization artifact of one response. It is NOT.
poll81_PERSISTENCE_CONFIRMED.measurement: 8721134 was re-fetched cold at 16:44, roughly 7 minutes after the poll-80 fetch. #865 FRANK VENEZIA's BestLapTime is still the literal string '00:01:'. The value is baked into the published record, not produced per-response.
poll81_PERSISTENCE_CONFIRMED.consequence: A consumer cannot retry its way out of this. Re-fetching returns the same malformed value, so a retry-on-parse-failure loop would spin without recovering, and a 'fetch again and take the newer copy' strategy is no defence either. The strict-pattern validation and typed malformed outcome prescribed in this entry's durableRule are the only mitigation.
poll81_PERSISTENCE_CONFIRMED.strictAuditThisFire: The anchored pattern ^\\d{2}:\\d{2}:\\d{2}\\.\\d{3}$ was applied programmatically to every BestLapTime, LastLapTime and TotalTime in BOTH siblings (24 + 22 competitor rows). Result: exactly one non-empty non-matching value, the known '00:01:'. Zero malformed TotalTime, zero malformed LastLapTime. This is the first time the audit prescribed by the durableRule has actually been RUN rather than asserted, and it confirms scopeCheck's 'rare, not endemic' on a second independent fetch.

widgetBlanksLastTimeForStoppedCars.observation: #201 PAUL SHAH (GTD2, P22, last) renders an EMPTY .lastTimeValue on every probe this fire, while simultaneously carrying Laps='2', BestLap='2' and BestTime='01:26.240'. He is the ONLY blank .lastTimeValue among 22 rows. He is 9 laps down on a 12-lap leader.
widgetBlanksLastTimeForStoppedCars.whyItIsNotThePriorFinding: lastTimeRenderedRowSubset and armedGridIsEmptyNotZero cover blank Last Time BEFORE a car has completed a lap -- an unstarted cell. This is different: the car HAS completed laps, its best lap is populated from lap 2, and the cell is blank anyway. A car that has stopped circulating therefore loses its Last Time while retaining every other value.
widgetBlanksLastTimeForStoppedCars.hypothesis: UNCONFIRMED. The most economical reading is that the widget clears Last Time once a car has failed to cross the line for some interval (pitted, retired, or off), so a blank Last Time on a car with Laps>0 means 'not currently circulating' rather than 'no data'. It could also be an unrelated per-car rendering fault. This fire cannot distinguish the two -- it has one car, one session.
widgetBlanksLastTimeForStoppedCars.whyItMattersForCameraControl: If the hypothesis holds, blank-Last-Time-with-Laps>0 is a usable per-car 'stopped' signal from the widget with no API dependency. If it does NOT hold, a consumer computing field-wide statistics over .lastTimeValue will silently skip cars. Either way the cell must not be treated as 'always populated once racing has started'.
widgetBlanksLastTimeForStoppedCars.howToTestNextTime: Watch a car that is known to pit under green and record whether its .lastTimeValue blanks, and how long after its last crossing. Also check whether it REPOPULATES if the car rejoins. Cross-check against the API's LastLapTime for the same car in the same instant -- note that 8721133 DOES carry LastLapTime 00:01:26.240 for #201 while the widget shows blank, so the two sources already disagree on this car.

poll81_FALSIFIED_AS_A_SHORT_TIMEOUT.verdict: The poll-80 hypothesis ('the widget clears Last Time once a car has failed to cross the line for some interval') is DISPROVED as a short-dwell timeout. It survives only in a much weaker long-dwell form, or not at all.
poll81_FALSIFIED_AS_A_SHORT_TIMEOUT.theFalsifyingCase: #125 PETER DEBUSMANN (GTD1) is frozen at Laps=9 with a BYTE-IDENTICAL Last Time of 01:27.749 across three observations spanning 6m30s: 16:40:56, 16:44:57 and 16:47:26. Over that same window his Diff accumulated from +6 laps to +8 laps, which independently confirms he is not circulating -- the field gained two laps on him while his own lap count did not move. He is unambiguously stopped and his Last Time is unambiguously populated.
poll81_FALSIFIED_AS_A_SHORT_TIMEOUT.whyThisIsACleanTest: It is a same-session, same-probe, same-selector comparison against #201, so no rendering-mode, layout or session-configuration difference can explain the divergence. Both cars are stopped; one blanks and one does not.
survivingHypotheses: LONG DWELL TIMEOUT: the blanking threshold is longer than 6m30s. #201 has been frozen at Laps=2 since at least 16:33:35 (>=13m51s at last probe) and #125 only since ~16:40 or earlier. Consistent with the data but requires the threshold to sit somewhere in (6m30s, 13m51s].
LAPS-DOWN THRESHOLD: the widget blanks Last Time for cars beyond some deficit. #201 is +15 laps; #125 is +8 laps. Also consistent, and does not require a timer at all.
poll81_FALSIFIED_AS_A_SHORT_TIMEOUT.howToDiscriminate: Watch #125 through to this session's checkered. Under the dwell model his Last Time should blank once his freeze exceeds ~14 minutes (i.e. by roughly 16:55, plausibly before the checkered). Under the laps-down model it should blank when his deficit crosses whatever #201 crossed, or never, since a stopped car's deficit grows at roughly one lap per 80s and he was at +8 at 16:47:26. The two models make DIFFERENT predictions for the same car in the same session, which is the ideal case. Record #125's Laps, Last Time and Diff on every remaining probe.
poll81_FALSIFIED_AS_A_SHORT_TIMEOUT.apiParityNote: The API retains LastLapTime for BOTH cars where the widget blanks one: 8721133 carries LastLapTime 00:01:26.240 for #201 (widget blank) and 00:01:28.151 for #51. So the blanking is a WIDGET rendering decision, not an upstream data loss, which rules out the 'unrelated per-car rendering fault' alternative only in the sense that it is definitely widget-side. Note 8721134 has LastLapTime wiped on all 22 cars, so use 8721133 for this cross-check, not the later sibling -- see apiLaterSiblingCanLoseData.
poll81_FALSIFIED_AS_A_SHORT_TIMEOUT.consumerRuleUnchanged: Regardless of which model wins, the operative rule stands and is now better evidenced: .lastTimeValue must NOT be treated as 'always populated once racing has started'. A consumer computing field-wide statistics over it will silently skip cars, and it cannot be used as a 'car is running' signal because a stopped car may render a stale time for at least 6m30s.

widgetClassCensusCanLoseAnEntireToken.severity: HIGH for any consumer that uses the widget class census as a SET; LOW for the any-token-membership run-group test currently in use.
widgetClassCensusCanLoseAnEntireToken.observation: The widget's distinct .racerCategory set over all 22 rows is ['', GT3, GTB1, GTC3, GTC6, GTC7, GTC8, GTD1, GTD2, STG] -- nine real tokens plus the empty string. The API's CategoryString for the same session is 'GT3 / GTB1 / GTC3 / GTC5 / GTC6 / GTC7 / GTC8 / GTD1 / GTD2 / STG' -- ten tokens. GTC5 is missing from the widget entirely.
widgetClassCensusCanLoseAnEntireToken.mechanism: #51 ROBERT HARGESHEIMER is the group's ONLY GTC5 entrant, and his row renders a blank .racerCategory. When the sole member of a class blanks its class cell, that class disappears from the widget-derived universe completely. There is no other row to carry the token.
widgetClassCensusCanLoseAnEntireToken.theMutationIsTheNewPart: widgetCanRenderABlankClassToken recorded the blank cell as an apparently static per-car sparseness ('the row is sparsely populated generally'). That framing is now wrong. #51 rendered the literal string 'GTC5' at 16:22:40 on the ARMED grid of THIS SAME SESSION, and blank at 16:41:39 and on both probes since. The class cell is MUTABLE within a session, so the widget's class census is time-varying and monotonically non-increasing within the observation so far.
widgetClassCensusCanLoseAnEntireToken.verification: Structural, not by eye: a scan of all 22 .racerCategory nodes returned exactly one blank, its sibling .racerName is '#51 ROBERT HARGESHEIMER', and the API's Categories dict resolves his Category id 7 to 'GTC5'. The prior 'GTC5' rendering is in the capture log at 2026-08-08T16:22:40 as the row string '7|#51 ROBERT HARGESHEIMER|GTC5'.
widgetClassCensusCanLoseAnEntireToken.whyTheCurrentTestSurvives: runGroupIdentificationByClassTokens uses ANY-token membership against each run group's universe. Nine surviving tokens still land uniquely in the Red universe, so identification was correct this fire. The test is robust to token loss precisely because it is existential rather than an equality check.
widgetClassCensusCanLoseAnEntireToken.whatWouldBreak: Any consumer doing set EQUALITY against a stored universe, computing a per-class car count, iterating classes to build per-class leaderboards, or asserting that the widget census matches the entry roster. All of those would silently report a nine-class race. Worse, the failure is intermittent: the same session showed ten classes 22 minutes earlier.
widgetClassCensusCanLoseAnEntireToken.durableRule: Never treat the widget .racerCategory census as the authoritative class roster. Use it only for existential run-group identification, with blanks filtered per widgetCanRenderABlankClassToken. For the actual class list use the API's session-level CategoryString (which runGroupIdentificationByClassTokens.poll75 already found is the un-culled ENTRY roster), and for a specific car's class use .Session.Categories[competitor.Category].Name. Both API paths were confirmed correct this fire on the exact car the widget dropped.
widgetClassCensusCanLoseAnEntireToken.relationToClaudeMdRules: Parallel Implementation Rule: widget and API are two implementations of 'what class is this car', and this is what a parity check between them catches -- a shared-contract property (the class token set) that the signature never captured and that the two sources disagree on, silently, in one direction only. Also the Data-Capture rule's dropped-with-reason discipline: the widget drops a field with no flag, so a consumer cannot distinguish 'no GTC5 entered' from 'GTC5 entered and was not rendered'.
widgetClassCensusCanLoseAnEntireToken.openQuestion: Cause of the blanking is unknown, and whether it ever REPOPULATES is untested. #51 is still circulating normally (lap 15, last 01:26.939 at 16:47:26), so this is NOT the same phenomenon as the stopped-car Last Time blanking -- a running car lost its class while keeping every timing value. Check at the checkered whether GTC5 returns to the census.

apiGroupObjectHasNoCategoryString.trap: In GroupedSessionsForRace, the GROUP object's key set is exactly {Category, Sessions}. There is NO CategoryString on the group. A jq filter reading .GroupedSessions[].CategoryString returns null for every group, silently, with .Successful true.
apiGroupObjectHasNoCategoryString.theConfusion: CategoryString DOES exist -- on the SESSION object, in both GroupedSessionsForRace and SessionDetails. The group's analogous field is named .Category and holds a '/'-joined class-token string that is textually identical to its sessions' CategoryString (e.g. 'GT3 / GTB1 / GTC3 / GTC5 / GTC6 / GTC7 / GTC8 / GTD1 / GTD2 / STG'). So the same VALUE lives under two different NAMES at two different levels.
apiGroupObjectHasNoCategoryString.extraHazard: 'Category' is now a THIRD distinct thing in this API under one name: (a) the group-level '/'-joined class-token string, (b) the competitor-level numeric-string id into the Categories dict, and (c) the Categories dict entries themselves. Three levels, one word, three different types (string-of-tokens, numeric string, object). apiCompetitorCategoryIsADictKeyNotAStringIndex covers the (b)/(c) confusion; this adds (a).
apiGroupObjectHasNoCategoryString.failureSignature: SILENT NULL, the house style of this API. The grouping key a consumer most naturally reaches for at the group level does not exist, and asking for it yields null rather than an error.
apiGroupObjectHasNoCategoryString.durableRule: To group sessions, key on the GROUP's .Category. To read a session's class roster, use the SESSION's .CategoryString. Never assume a field name carries across nesting levels in this API -- enumerate the key set at each level (keys: group={Category,Sessions}; session=11 keys per apiSessionDetailsSchemaTrap.sessionKeyUnion; competitor=18 keys per apiCompetitorSchema).
apiGroupObjectHasNoCategoryString.relationToClaudeMdRules: Syntactic-Semantic Seam Rule: one semantic distinction ('which class group is this') with two names and three types depending on where you stand in the tree, and no single canonical representation. Also the Data-Capture rule: the three-level key enumeration recorded here is what should have been done before writing the extractor.

redSprint2FinishedAtEvidence.confirmedStableAt: 2026-08-08T17:00:08-04:00 -- second probe, byte-identical header (clock 00:00:00, ttg 00:00:00, ltg 0, flag ''), grid frozen.

apiGroupedSessionsTopLevelKeyTrap.finding: The GroupedSessionsForRace response's top-level keys are exactly [Favorited, GroupedSessions, Successful]. There is no .Groups. A consumer that writes [.Groups[]?.Sessions[]?] gets an EMPTY ARRAY and no error, because ?-suffixed iteration over null yields nothing.
apiGroupedSessionsTopLevelKeyTrap.whyItMatters: This is the fourth independent way this one endpoint pair can silently report an empty race, alongside apiEndpointPathTrap (wrong /v2/ prefix -> HTML with a 200), apiWrongKeySilentZero (.Competitors instead of .SortedCompetitors), and apiSessionSchemaFieldTraps (.SessionID/.SessionEpoch are null; the real fields are .ID and .SessionStartDateEpoc). All four fail OPEN -- a plausible empty result, never an exception.
apiGroupedSessionsTopLevelKeyTrap.compoundHazard: The schema-field trap is the nastiest of the four because it does not produce an empty result, it produces a WRONG ORDER. sort_by(.SessionEpoch) over records whose .SessionEpoch is uniformly null is a stable no-op, so the 'newest sessions' slice returned this fire was actually alphabetical-by-group order and looked entirely plausible (it listed Practice 3 / Qualifying / Sprint 1 / Sprint 2 / Sprint 2 / Warm-Up). Sorting on the real key .SessionStartDateEpoc gave a materially different list. Any session-selection logic built on the null field would silently pick the wrong session.
apiGroupedSessionsTopLevelKeyTrap.durableRule: For every field this API is indexed on, assert non-null across the whole collection before sorting or selecting on it -- an all-null sort key must be a hard error, not a silent identity sort. Confirmed real key names: response.GroupedSessions[].Sessions[] with .ID, .Name, .CategoryString, .SessionStartDateEpoc (note the truncated spelling), .SessionDate, .SessionTime, .SortMode, .Categories, .RaceID, .ResultsProcessorVersion; and SessionDetails -> .Session.SortedCompetitors.

racerNameFusesNumberAndDriver.discovered: 2026-08-08T17:14-04:00 (poll 83), frozen Red Sprint 2 final grid, 22 rows
racerNameFusesNumberAndDriver.finding: There is NO '.number' cell and NO '.name' cell in a leaderboard row. A scoped row.querySelector('.number') and row.querySelector('.name') each returned null for 22 of 22 rows. The car number is FUSED into '.racerName' as a single string: '#17 MARK CALZARETTA'. The run-group class token lives in a sibling span '.racerCategory' ('GTC8\r').
racerNameFusesNumberAndDriver.fullRowCellCensus: Complete class-token census taken over all 22 rows; every one of these 25 tokens resolved in 22/22 rows: racerRowStacked (row), racerRowHighlight, positionContainer, position, racerRowItem, row1, row2, row3, racerName, racerCategory, additionalData, racerRowLabel, racerRowValue, and the label/value pairs lapsLabel/lapsValue, lastTimeLabel/lastTimeValue, bestLapLabel/bestLapValue, bestTimeLabel/bestTimeValue, diffLabel/diffValue, gapLabel/gapValue, plus alignRight. No row has a missing NODE; blanks are always empty TEXT.
racerNameFusesNumberAndDriver.durableRule: Extract the car number by parsing '.racerName', not by looking for a number cell. The observed shape is /^#(\S+)\s+(.*)$/ across all 22 rows (numbers observed include leading-zero forms '01', '029', '8', '333' -- so the number is a STRING, never parse it as an integer or the leading zeros are silently destroyed and '01' collides with '1').
racerNameFusesNumberAndDriver.relationToClaudeMdRules: Syntactic-Semantic Seam Rule. 'Which car is this?' is a semantic distinction the DOM does not carry in its own field -- it is recoverable only by splitting a display string. A consumer must own that split in one place, not re-encode '#(\d+)' at every call site, and must keep the number as a string.
racerNameFusesNumberAndDriver.howTheErrorWouldHaveShipped: row.querySelector('.name') returns null, not an error. A naive extractor emits 22 rows with name=null and number=null and looks like it worked -- the row count, positions, laps and times are all correct. Same silent-null family as apiWrongKeySilentZero, arriving on the DOM side.

fabricatedRowSelectorSilentZero_poll83.whatHappened: This fire opened by selecting rows with div[class*="timingRow"] -- a plausible-sounding class name invented from the header's real 'timingHeader' class. It matched 0 elements against a fully-rendered 22-car grid. The probe returned rowCount:0 with no error and no warning.
fabricatedRowSelectorSilentZero_poll83.whyItIsWorthRecording: rowSelectorCensus (poll 73) already documented that the substring form over-counts ~18x and the exact-token form 'racerRow' returns 0. This is a THIRD failure mode: a selector that is neither -- simply a wrong name -- and it also returns 0. The 'assert the count against an independent witness' rule is what caught it: .position node count was 22, .racerRowStacked was 22, div[class*=timingRow] was 0. Two of three agreed.
fabricatedRowSelectorSilentZero_poll83.durableRule: Never accept a zero-row result as 'the session is empty'. Zero rows must be cross-checked against an independent witness (.position node count, or body innerText length -- 2987 chars here, obviously non-empty) before any consumer concludes there is no field. Per the No-Log-Scraping rule, collapsing a selector miss into 'session not running' is exactly the inference that must not be made.
fabricatedRowSelectorSilentZero_poll83.confirmedSelector: .racerRowStacked -> 22 rows; distinct className set across all row elements is exactly ['racerRowStacked'], unchanged from poll 73's finding on a 29-car armed grid.

trailingCrIsALiveFeedArtifactNotApi.finding: The trailing carriage return that appears throughout the widget is NOT present anywhere in the REST results payload for the same session. Direct census on session 8721134 (Red Sprint 2, 22 competitors): ZERO of 22 .AdditionalData values and ZERO of 22 .Nationality values contain a \r. In the widget, at the same moment, 21 of 22 .racerCategory cells and 20 of 22 .additionalData cells DO carry a trailing \r.
trailingCrIsALiveFeedArtifactNotApi.consequence: The CR is introduced by the widget's live-timing transport (or by the widget's own rendering of it), not by the source data as the results API serves it. It follows that trailingCarriageReturnFieldSubset and sessionNameTrailingCarriageReturn are describing a property of the LIVE path only.
trailingCrIsALiveFeedArtifactNotApi.durableRule: Strip trailing \r defensively on every string read from the widget DOM, and do NOT expect the same strings from the REST API to need it. Crucially, do not use presence-of-CR as a discriminator, a checksum, or a source-identifier -- it is a transport artifact that differs by path and is absent on 1-2 of 22 rows even within the live path.
theTwoCrLessWidgetRows: #113 KATZ -- .additionalData 'WHITE/RED/BLACK / 05 996' has no CR but is COMPLETE. So CR-absence does not imply data loss.
#51 HARGESHEIMER -- .additionalData 'WHITE' and .racerCategory '' both CR-less AND both truncated. See neitherSourceIsASupersetForEntryMetadata.
trailingCrIsALiveFeedArtifactNotApi.whatIsNOTClaimed: No claim about WHERE in the live path the CR is inserted. The widget's live transport was not inspected this fire; only its rendered output was compared against the REST payload. The CR could originate in the timing hardware feed, a relay, or the widget's own string handling.
trailingCrIsALiveFeedArtifactNotApi.revises: sessionNameTrailingCarriageReturn, trailingCarriageReturnFieldSubset -- both should now be read as scoped to the widget/live path. The 'structuralHypothesis' recorded under trailingCarriageReturnFieldSubset (that the CR marks a particular subset of source fields) is weakened: the REST API serves those same fields CR-free.

neitherSourceIsASupersetForEntryMetadata.finding: For the SAME session (Red Sprint 2), the widget and the REST API each hold entry metadata the other is missing, on different rows. Loss runs in opposite directions, so neither source can be treated as authoritative or as a superset.
evidence: #51 HARGESHEIMER -- widget: .racerCategory '' and .additionalData 'WHITE'. API: Category=7 (GTC5), Nationality='WHITE', AdditionalData='11 997.2 CUP'. The API has strictly more.
#201 SHAH -- widget: .additionalData 'WHITE / 19 718 CAYMAN CLUBSPORT'. API: Nationality='WHITE', AdditionalData='19 7'. The widget has strictly more; the API value looks truncated mid-token.
Every other row agrees: the widget's .additionalData is exactly Nationality + ' / ' + AdditionalData.
neitherSourceIsASupersetForEntryMetadata.compositionRule: widget .additionalData == API Nationality + ' / ' + API AdditionalData, EXCEPT that the widget omits the separator and the second half when its own AdditionalData is empty (#51 renders bare 'WHITE'). Note 'Nationality' is a misnomer -- it carries the car's LIVERY/colour string ('BLUE', 'WHITE/RED/BLACK', 'GREEN/BLACK'), which is exactly the false-positive source that makes a body-text colour-word grep useless for flag detection (see textGrepIsInsufficient).

twoReadings.A_operatorEditsDuringSession: The API stub froze ~6 laps in; the widget is the post-session final. #201's '19 7' could be the timing operator mid-typing at stub time, later completed -- which the widget then shows in full. That reading is natural for #201 but awkward for #51, where the widget would have had to LOSE data it once had.
twoReadings.B_independentLossPaths: The two transports drop fields independently. Supported by the CR result above (the paths demonstrably differ in their string handling) and by apiSiblingRecordsAreNotIdentical / apiLaterSiblingCanLoseData, which already show the API alone losing fields between its own siblings.
twoReadings.status: PARTLY RESOLVED. #51 = reading B (widget-side mid-session loss, established by poll 81's arm-time capture plus poll 83's API cross-reference). #201's API truncation still unexplained. Neither-is-a-superset stands on both rows regardless.
twoReadings.SELF_CORRECTION_poll83b: The 'status: UNRESOLVED' above was written without re-reading notes item (1) from poll 81, which ALREADY performed the decisive test. The widget rendered 'GTC5' for #51 at 16:22:40 (armed) and blank by 16:41:39 -- a MID-SESSION MUTATION in the widget. So for #51 the answer is reading B: the widget genuinely lost a value it had previously displayed. What poll 83 adds is the independent confirmation of the TRUE value from a second source (API Category=7 -> Categories['7'].Name == 'GTC5'), upgrading widgetClassCensusCanLoseAnEntireToken from a set-difference inference to a directly cross-referenced fact. #201's API-side truncation ('19 7') remains unexplained and could still be reading A. The durable merge rule is unchanged.

neitherSourceIsASupersetForEntryMetadata.durableRule: Entry metadata (number, driver, class, livery, car) must be MERGED across widget and API, keyed on car number as a STRING, taking the non-empty value from either side and flagging disagreements. Never fill a missing field with '' or a default -- carry it as explicitly unknown, per the No-Log-Scraping rule (a blank must not be inferred into a category).
neitherSourceIsASupersetForEntryMetadata.relationToClaudeMdRules: Parallel Implementation Rule, applied to two data SOURCES rather than two code implementations: the widget and the REST API are substitutable-looking providers of the same entity, and the properties their shared shape does not capture -- which fields can be blank, which can be truncated, whether strings carry a CR -- diverge silently. Neither source errors; each just quietly has a different answer.
neitherSourceIsASupersetForEntryMetadata.severityForCameraControl: Medium-high. Any rule of the form 'shoot cars in class X' or 'label frames with driver/car' reads exactly these fields, and both sources will hand back a confident wrong-or-empty answer for at least one car per session.
